questions: Distinguish progress from heartbeat and fixed ceilings from per-command idle windows.
Check Windows/POSIX descendant cleanup, CPU false progress and quiet remote I/O.
decision: Keep per-command sliding progress windows distinct from hard ceilings and liveness; strengthen semantic progress and process-tree tests.
code_observations: progress_signal distinguishes PROGRESS, ERROR and HEARTBEAT. progress_watch and process_tree support output/metrics/file signals and descendant cleanup.
The configuration already separates task idle timeout, validation idle windows and hard ceilings. Zero values have documented disable/default behavior that must not be silently changed.
implementation_steps: Prefer completed-work counters or pinned progress files/probes over arbitrary changing text. Heartbeats and watcher telemetry must not refresh semantic progress.
Treat CPU activity as supporting evidence, not proof that useful work advances; test busy loops and silent remote I/O separately.
Use monotonic clocks for durations and bounded read-only probes. Preserve expected quiet periods without extending an explicit hard ceiling.
On cancellation/timeout, terminate the owned tree and drain remaining output safely. Use Windows Job Objects and POSIX process ownership primitives through their tested platform adapters.
Record the exact timeout class and last meaningful progress evidence. A hard ceiling is blocked-for-review, not proof a stronger model is needed.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Repeated heartbeat-only output does not keep a stalled command alive.
Increasing completed-work counters renew idle time while a fixed hard ceiling still wins.
Each command starts a new idle window; the validation set has no unintended aggregate timeout.
A child scheduled to write later cannot escape timeout cleanup on supported Windows/POSIX runs.
A CPU-busy infinite loop and a quiet but externally advancing operation produce distinct diagnostic evidence.

alternatives.title: Raise every timeout after a stall
alternatives.tradeoff: Quick workaround but hides deadlocks and spends quota/time without evidence.

alternatives.title: Semantic progress plus separate ceilings and owned cleanup
alternatives.tradeoff: More precise failure diagnosis with bounded monitoring overhead.

alternatives.title: Treat any log line or CPU increment as progress
alternatives.tradeoff: Allows infinite noisy loops and confuses liveness with useful work.

cost_model: Measure false-stall and missed-stall rates, cancellation latency and probe overhead. Do not activate an expensive model merely because five minutes elapsed.
unverified: Real descendant behavior, permissions and breakaway processes require platform CI. A fake process test only covers the configured contract.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated model calls; tests listed here are implementation obligations, not claimed passes.
